title: Bastidas explores the isthmus
description: Rodrigo de Bastidas sails along the Caribbean coast, the first European to see the isthmus.

title: Columbus names Portobelo
description: Sheltering on his fourth voyage, Columbus names the harbour that becomes the treasure port of the isthmus.

title: Santa María la Antigua founded
description: Survivors of Ojeda's colony found the first lasting Spanish town on the American mainland, governed by Vasco Núñez de Balboa.

title: Balboa sees the Pacific
place: Darién (summit unknown; shown at Santa María la Antigua)
description: Crossing the isthmus, Balboa looks down from a hill and becomes the first European to sight the Pacific from the Americas.

title: Panama City founded
description: Pedrarias Dávila founds the first European city on the Pacific coast of the Americas.

title: Morgan sacks Panama City
description: Henry Morgan's buccaneers seize the richest city on the Pacific coast, and it burns in the sack.

title: New city built
description: The city is rebuilt on a peninsula at the mouth of the bay, the modern Casco Viejo.

title: Independence from Spain
description: Without a shot, the notables of Panama City declare separation from Spain and join Gran Colombia.

title: State of the Isthmus
description: During a Colombian civil war Panama declares itself a free state; it rejoins the union thirteen months later.

title: First transcontinental railway
description: The Panama Railroad opens across the isthmus, making it the shortcut between the oceans in the California gold rush.

title: Watermelon Riot
description: A dispute at the railway station over a ten-cent watermelon escalates into a melee that kills American passengers and sparks a US occupation.

title: French canal attempt
description: De Lesseps's French company starts digging a sea-level canal; disease kills tens of thousands and the company collapses in ruin.

title: Hay–Bunau-Varilla Treaty
description: Fifteen days after separation from Colombia, the new republic grants the United States a Zone in perpetuity to build the canal.

title: Canal opens
description: The first ocean-going ship crosses the canal, joining the Atlantic and Pacific by water.

title: Martyrs' Day
description: Clashes over flying the Panamanian flag in the Zone leave about twenty Panamanians dead and set the sovereignty movement aflame.

title: Torrijos coup
description: The National Guard departs the elected president after eleven days, installing Omar Torrijos.

title: Torrijos–Carter Treaties
description: Torrijos and President Carter sign the treaties that promise the canal to Panama at the end of the century.

title: Death of Torrijos
description: The general dies when his plane crashes into a mountain, leaving the Guard to Noriega.

title: Noriega takes command
description: Manuel Noriega becomes head of the Panamanian Defense Forces and the real ruler of the country.

title: United States invasion
description: More than twenty thousand American troops depose Noriega in four days of fighting.

title: Mireya Moscoso elected
description: Moscoso wins the presidency and becomes the first woman to hold it.

title: Canal handover
description: At noon the last vestige of the Canal Zone ends and Panama takes over the canal and its bases.

title: Expansion referendum
description: Voters approve the plan to build a third, wider lane of locks.

title: Expanded canal opens
description: The new locks take their first ship, nearly doubling the canal's capacity.
